summary:
I merged the three input lists, which were identical: 74 unique (district, award) rows from JSJB 1.0, the only JSJB award round so far. The President and the Minister conferred these awards on 18 Nov 2025 at Vigyan Bhawan, alongside the 6th National Water Awards.

I verified every row against two official sources:
1. The PIB release of 11 Nov 2025 (PRID 2188706), titled 'Recognition of Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari (JSJB) Award Winners under Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain'. I fetched it with curl; all 74 names appear in its annexure, and its text states '67 Districts, six municipal corporations, one urban local body'.
2. The DoWR awardee PDF at https://www.jalshakti-dowr.gov.in/static/uploads/2025/11/33c8968f7421c53f2e85fc72b3ed95de.pdf. I parsed it in raw mode, and every zone, category, rank, completed-works count and prize matched.

No input row had to be dropped.

The 74 rows break down as follows:
- 14 Category 1 districts (Rs 2 crore each, conferred by the President)
- 10 Category 2 districts (Rs 1 crore each)
- 43 Category 3 districts (Rs 25 lakh each)
- 6 municipal corporations: Raipur, Hyderabad (HMWS&SB), Gorakhpur, Rajahmundry, Ghaziabad, Surat
- 1 urban local body: Guna (Rs 40 lakh)

Three districts appear twice, as both a district award and an urban-body award: Raipur, Surat and Guna. That leaves 70 distinct district names for the queue. Two district assignments are my own inference: Hyderabad MC is mapped to Hyderabad district, and Rajahmundry MC to East Godavari. Name normalisations: East Nimar = Khandwa; Jangoan = Jangaon; SPSR Nellore is kept as the source gives it.

Completeness search, as of 17 Nov 2026: I found no JSJB 2.0 award winners and no 7th National Water Awards winners yet. The 7th awards (nominations closed 28 Aug 2026) include JSJB sub-categories, so a later run should check for new rows once those winners are announced.

The dropped list covers names that other sources link to JSJB but that are not JSJB district awards:
- National Water Awards Best District wins: Tirunelveli and Sepahijala.
- JSJB 2.0 and 3.0 progress rankings: Banaskantha, Salem and Kabirdham.
- Nodal-officer district clusters, which are awards to individual CWC/CGWB officers.
- The three state-level awards.
